repo.description:
## Summary

Revoking an organization member suspends them in the UI and hides organization items from their
sync, but does not remove the collection and group grants that the per-item authorization checks
rely on. A revoked member who keeps their own account can continue to read organization ciphers
one at a time, and can soft-delete and permanently delete them, indefinitely. The item-level checks
never consult membership status, while the listing queries do.

## Severity / CVSS

CVSS 3.1 vector: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N`
Base score: 8.1
Severity: High

`PR:L` because the attacker authenticates with their own surviving account, which revocation does
not disable. `C:H` for continued read access to organization secrets, including secrets rotated in
place after the revocation. `I:H` for permanent destruction of organization items; editing item
contents is blocked by a separate check, so this metric covers deletion only. `A:N` because the
service itself is unaffected.

## Affected component

- `src/db/models/cipher.rs`, `Cipher::get_access_restrictions`,
  `get_user_collections_access_flags`, `get_group_collections_access_flags`
- `src/db/models/group.rs`, `Group::is_in_full_access_group`
- `src/api/core/organizations.rs`, `revoke_member_impl`
- `src/api/core/ciphers.rs`, `get_cipher`, `delete_cipher_by_uuid`, `restore_cipher_by_uuid`,
  `delete_cipher_attachment_by_id`

Tested at commit `46ae59eaf444f0ae0a799070cf2bd6c415284a51`, default configuration, sqlite,
mail disabled.

## Root cause

Revocation adjusts the status field and saves the row:

```rust
// organizations.rs:2338, revoke_member_impl
member.revoke();          // status -= 128
member.save(conn).await?;
```

`Membership::save` (`organization.rs:752`) writes the membership row and nothing else. The removal
path, `Membership::delete` (`organization.rs:785`), does tear down the derived grants:

```rust
CollectionUser::delete_all_by_user_and_org(&self.user_uuid, &self.org_uuid, conn).await?;
GroupUser::delete_all_by_member(&self.uuid, conn).await?;
```

Revocation performs neither, so the `users_collections` and `groups_users` rows survive.

The listing queries compensate by filtering on membership status. `Cipher::find_by_user` joins
`users_organizations` under `status = Confirmed` and then constrains the collection join to that
membership:

```rust
// cipher.rs:814-825
.left_join(
    users_organizations::table.on(ciphers::organization_uuid
        .eq(users_organizations::org_uuid.nullable())
        .and(users_organizations::user_uuid.eq(user_uuid))
        .and(users_organizations::status.eq(MembershipStatus::Confirmed as i32))),
)
.left_join(
    users_collections::table.on(ciphers_collections::collection_uuid
        .eq(users_collections::collection_uuid)
        // Ensure that users_collections::user_uuid is NULL for unconfirmed users.
        .and(users_organizations::user_uuid.eq(users_collections::user_uuid))),
)
```

`Collection::find_by_user_uuid` filters status the same way (`collection.rs:258,295`), and
`Cipher::is_in_full_access_org` goes through `Membership::find_confirmed_by_user_and_org`
(`cipher.rs:566`).

The per-item authorization path does not. `get_user_collections_access_flags` joins
`ciphers` to `ciphers_collections` to `users_collections` on `user_uuid` alone and never touches
`users_organizations`, so membership status cannot be considered:

```rust
// cipher.rs:671-679
ciphers::table
    .filter(ciphers::uuid.eq(&self.uuid))
    .inner_join(ciphers_collections::table.on(ciphers::uuid.eq(ciphers_collections::cipher_uuid)))
    .inner_join(
        users_collections::table.on(ciphers_collections::collection_uuid
            .eq(users_collections::collection_uuid)
            .and(users_collections::user_uuid.eq(user_uuid))),
    )
    .select((users_collections::read_only, users_collections::hide_passwords, users_collections::manage))
```

The two group paths, `get_group_collections_access_flags` (`cipher.rs:686`) and
`Group::is_in_full_access_group` (`group.rs:269`), do join `users_organizations`, but they filter it
on `users_organizations::user_uuid` alone and never add the `status` predicate, so a revoked
member's group grants resolve the same way a confirmed member's do.

`Cipher::get_access_restrictions` therefore returns `Some(flags)` for a revoked member, and every
endpoint keyed on it still grants access. Those endpoints take the plain `Headers` guard, so
`OrgHeaders`, which does reject revoked members, never runs:

```rust
// ciphers.rs:225-233
#[get("/ciphers/<cipher_id>")]
async fn get_cipher(cipher_id: CipherId, headers: Headers, conn: DbConn) -> JsonResult {
    let Some(cipher) = Cipher::find_by_uuid(&cipher_id, &conn).await else {
        err!("Cipher doesn't exist")
    };
    if !cipher.is_accessible_to_user(&headers.user.uuid, &conn).await {
        err!("Cipher is not owned by user")
    }
```

A revoked Admin, Owner, or `access_all` member is correctly blocked, because those resolve through
`find_confirmed_by_user_and_org`. Only members holding explicit collection or group grants are
affected, which is the ordinary configuration for regular users.

## Impact

An organization revokes a member, for example when offboarding an employee. The web vault shows
the member as revoked and their sync no longer returns organization items. With their own
unchanged credentials they can still:

- read any organization cipher whose id they know, including the password field, using
  `GET /api/ciphers/<id>`. Every member has those ids from their pre-revocation sync.
- soft-delete organization ciphers with `PUT /api/ciphers/<id>/delete`.
- permanently delete them with `DELETE /api/ciphers/<id>`, after which the owner's own fetch fails.
- delete attachments, and restore soft-deleted items.

Editing cipher contents is blocked, by a separate check rather than by the authorization gate.

Two points make this worse than a stale copy of data the member already synced.

Rotating organization secrets is the standard response to an offboarding, and rotating a Bitwarden
item in place keeps its id. The revoked member reads the new value from the same
`GET /api/ciphers/<id>` they used before, so the usual remediation does not close the exposure.
Only moving a secret to a newly created item, whose id they never saw, puts it out of reach.

Revocation is also silent about its own failure. The administrator sees the member at status `-1`
and an empty sync for them, with no indication that item access continues.

Revocation does not touch the user account, the security stamp, or issued tokens. Existing sessions
keep working and re-authentication works, so there is no window after which this lapses.

## Proof of Concept

Build and run a stock instance from the tested commit:

```
cargo build --no-default-features --features sqlite

DATA_FOLDER=./data DATABASE_URL=sqlite://./data/db.sqlite3 \
ROCKET_ADDRESS=127.0.0.1 ROCKET_PORT=8000 DOMAIN=http://127.0.0.1:8000 \
SIGNUPS_ALLOWED=true WEB_VAULT_ENABLED=false \
./target/debug/vaultwarden
```

The attached `revoked-member-retains-access.sh` registers an owner and a member, creates an
organization, a collection, and a login cipher, invites the member as type User with that one
collection at `readOnly: false`, confirms them, then revokes them. Client-side crypto is not
required: vaultwarden stores the master password hash and key blobs without interpreting them, so
fixed placeholder strings exercise the server's authorization logic.

The member's role matters when reproducing. Use type User with an explicit collection grant, which
is the ordinary configuration. A revoked Admin, Owner, or member with `access_all` resolves through
`Membership::find_confirmed_by_user_and_org` and is correctly denied, so testing with one of those
accounts will not reproduce this.

```
$ bash run.sh
vaultwarden up (pid 4013343), default config, mail disabled

== setup ==
org:          cdca5169-f760-45f8-baa6-c69769da9cbb
collection:   9982ddd2-d276-44fb-beca-ed066e063a27
cipher:       bc3af6cf-4282-43af-9f00-0671ec09b810
membership:   dd977d92-d22f-4c54-9ffa-285d29217cdc
status now:   2  (2 = Confirmed)

== before revocation ==
member GET /api/ciphers/bc3af6cf-...            -> 200
member sync lists the org cipher                -> 1

== owner revokes the member ==
PUT /api/organizations/cdca5169-.../users/dd977d92-.../revoke -> 200
status now:   -1  (API reports -1 for revoked; the row stores 2 - 128 = -126)

== after revocation, same member token ==
member sync lists the org cipher                -> 0
member GET /api/ciphers/bc3af6cf-...            -> 200
password field returned to revoked member       -> 2.aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa
member PUT /api/ciphers/bc3af6cf-...            -> 400
  reason: You don't have permission to add item to organization

== fresh login by the revoked member (no stale token) ==
member GET /api/ciphers/bc3af6cf-...            -> 200

== deletion by the revoked member ==
member PUT /api/ciphers/bc3af6cf-.../delete (soft) -> 200
owner sees deletedDate                          -> 2026-07-28T02:57:50.002195Z
member DELETE /api/ciphers/bc3af6cf-... (hard)  -> 200
owner GET /api/ciphers/bc3af6cf-...             -> 400
```

The sync listing returns 0 while the direct fetch returns 200 with the cipher body in the same
session, which isolates the difference to the per-item check. The fresh login shows this is not a
stale-token artefact. The final two lines show the item is gone for the owner as well.

## Recommended fix

Make the per-item access checks require a confirmed membership, the way the listing queries already
do.

In `get_user_collections_access_flags`, join `users_organizations` and filter on it:

```rust
.inner_join(users_organizations::table.on(ciphers::organization_uuid
    .eq(users_organizations::org_uuid.nullable())
    .and(users_organizations::user_uuid.eq(user_uuid))
    .and(users_organizations::status.eq(MembershipStatus::Confirmed as i32))))
```

Apply the same filter in `get_group_collections_access_flags` and
`Group::is_in_full_access_group`, which already join `users_organizations` and need only the
additional `status` predicate. `Collection::find_by_uuid_and_user`, `is_writable_by_user`, and
`is_coll_manageable_by_user` have the same gap.

Alternatively, or in addition, have `revoke_member_impl` clear the derived grants the way
`Membership::delete` does. That changes what restore has to rebuild, so filtering on status is the
smaller change.

## References

Commit tested: `46ae59eaf444f0ae0a799070cf2bd6c415284a51`

- `src/db/models/cipher.rs:597-733` (`get_access_restrictions` and the two flag helpers),
  `:555-571` (`is_in_full_access_org`), `:804-897` (`find_by_user`, which does filter status)
- `src/db/models/group.rs:269-285` (`is_in_full_access_group`)
- `src/db/models/collection.rs:258,295` (status filtered), `:350,432,570` (not filtered)
- `src/db/models/organization.rs:288-294` (`revoke`), `:752-783` (`save`), `:785-797` (`delete`)
- `src/api/core/organizations.rs:2315-2356` (`revoke_member_impl`)
- `src/api/core/ciphers.rs:225-236` (`get_cipher`), `:1779` (`delete_cipher_by_uuid`),
  `:1866` (`restore_cipher_by_uuid`), `:1938` (`delete_cipher_attachment_by_id`),
  `:449-451` (the confirmed-membership check that blocks editing)
- `src/auth.rs:766-814` (`OrgHeaders`, which rejects revoked members but does not guard these routes)
repo.summary: Revoked or unconfirmed organization member retains read and delete access to organization ciphers
